column10: If `runAnalyzer` returns valid JSON that is `null` (i.e., the binary outputs the string `"null"`), `JSON.parse` succeeds and `map` is assigned `null`. The try-catch block covers only the parse call, so the immediately following `map.fileActivity` access at line 63 throws an uncaught `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. This propagates to the caller as an unhandled exception instead of the graceful `{ available: false, error: '...' }` return. A null/type guard on `map` after parsing is needed.

`DEFAULT_OPTIONS.cwd` is evaluated once at module-load time via `process.cwd()`. Inside `collectGitData`, `opts.cwd` is always set to this stale value (since the spread always picks it up from `DEFAULT_OPTIONS`), making the `|| process.cwd()` fallback on line 36 dead code. Any caller that relies on the default cwd but invokes `collectGitData` after the process has changed working directory will silently analyse the wrong directory.

`binary.ensureBinarySync()` is called explicitly on line 37 (return value discarded), and then called a second time internally by `binary.runAnalyzer()` on line 47 (which always starts with `const binPath = ensureBinarySync()`). This redundant double-check is wasteful—`ensureBinarySync` can trigger a blocking child-process download. More importantly, if the binary disappears between the two calls, the second failure is caught by the wrong try-catch and surfaces as `'Git analysis failed'` instead of `'Binary not available'`.

The `adjustForAi` option is declared in `DEFAULT_OPTIONS`, documented in the JSDoc (`@param {boolean} [options.adjustForAi=false] - Adjust bus factor for AI commits`), and accepted by callers, but it is never read anywhere in the function body. The bus factor calculation always ignores AI attribution regardless of this flag. Callers passing `adjustForAi: true` will silently get the same result as the default, violating the documented contract.

The JSDoc for `collect()` lists `'github'`, `'docs'`, `'code'`, and `'docs-patterns'` as valid collector names but omits `'git'`. The `data` object initialises `git: null` unconditionally, meaning every collected payload now always includes a `git` key (valued `null`) even when no git collection is requested. Consumers that check for the presence of keys to determine what was collected will see a spurious `git` entry on every response.

The `aiRatio` calculation is flawed. It calculates `totalCommits` from only human contributors, but `allCommits` can fall back to this human-only total. The `aiTotal` is then divided by a potentially human-only `allCommits`, which can lead to an inflated and incorrect AI ratio if `map.git.totalCommitsAnalyzed` is not present. The total should consistently include both human and AI commits for an accurate ratio.

The returned object redundantly includes a top-level `busFactor` property, which is already nested inside the `health` object as `health.busFactor`. This creates an inconsistent and slightly bloated API surface.
The 'binary.ensureBinarySync()' call does not provide a way to recover or retry on failure. This could make the function brittle in scenarios where the binary is temporarily unavailable.
The 'binary.runAnalyzer' call assumes the output is valid JSON without handling cases where the binary might produce malformed data or unexpected output.
The hotspots calculation does not handle ties in the number of changes when sorting files, which could lead to inconsistent results.
The 'conventions' extraction assumes that 'style', 'prefixes', and 'scopes' exist in the map, which could lead to runtime errors if these keys are missing or unexpectedly formatted.
The 'cwd' parameter passed to 'binary.runAnalyzer' is not sanitized or validated, introducing the risk of issues if an invalid path is provided.
The 'humanList' sorting assumes that all contributors have a commitCount value, which might not hold true in edge cases. This could result in a crash or incorrect sorting.
The integration of the 'git' collector in the collect function assumes that the 'git.collectGitData' method always returns a well-formed object. There is no fallback mechanism in case of failure.

This runs `git-map init` through `execFileSync` without passing any `maxBuffer` or timeout options. `git-map init` returns a full repository map, so repositories whose JSON output exceeds Node's default exec buffer will make this collector report `available: false`, and long analyses can block indefinitely; pass explicit execution limits sized for this output.

The new git collector and index integration are not covered by tests, while the existing collectors and `collect()` routing have dedicated test coverage in `__tests__/collectors*.test.js` and `tests/collectors/collectors.test.js`. Please add tests for the binary failure path, parsed metric extraction, and selecting `collectors: ['git']` so this new collector's contract is protected.
